currentContext.strengths: Scale leadership: described as India's largest digital platform for truck operators, engaging ~1.1 million truck operators, of whom 818,259 were average monthly transacting truck operators|Network effects and multi-service stickiness: monthly transacting users using two or more services rose from 259,011 (FY24) to 339,701 (FY25) to 411,765 (FY26)|High engagement / switching cost: average daily time spent on the app by transacting customers of 43.76 minutes, with the app embedded in daily trucking workflows|Omnichannel distribution moat: a physical network of over 10,000+ touchpoints with presence across 80%+ districts, complementing digital channels, field sales, telesales and channel partners|Leadership in commercial vehicle tolling payments - described as the largest tolling platform in India|Proprietary data advantage across payments, vehicle locations, freight and credit, feeding product development and credit underwriting|Repeatable playbook for launching new offerings (Payments 2019, Telematics 2021, Loads 2023, Vehicle Financing 2023), lowering incremental customer acquisition cost|Scalable, asset-light model with in-house microservices technology, recurring revenue and high contribution margins giving operating leverage|Promoter-led management team and experienced board
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen the core businesses of Payments and Telematics while accelerating investment in the growth businesses of Loads and Vehicle Financing, so that each additional service makes the platform more valuable as operators adopt more offerings.|Build the digital infrastructure that lets truck operators manage their business and grow their earnings - an ambition explicitly framed as going beyond running successful individual businesses.|Operating model held constant since inception: identify real customer problems, solve them through a deeply engaged technology platform, and scale them through the omnichannel distribution network.|Integrate AI into products, using the Company's deep customer engagement and ecosystem understanding to apply these technologies to real-world customer problems.|Compete as India's largest digital platform for truck operators across an ecosystem spanning payments (tolling and fueling), telematics, loads and sourcing of financing for commercial vehicles, riding continued industry formalisation.
currentContext.expansion: BlackBuck is an asset-light digital platform, so its expansion narrative is footprint, distribution and platform build-out rather than plants or capacity. The Company frames it as 'Our Priorities for the Next Mile', built on five growth pillars. Expand Our Reach: strengthen market presence through strategic geographic expansion and deeper market penetration, increasing accessibility of the offerings to a larger segment of Indian truck operators to grow the transacting user base. Strengthen Our Foundations: keep investing in Payments and Telematics - the most frequently used offerings - while strengthening the technology infrastructure required to support scale, uptime and reliability. Accelerate New Growth Engines: expand marketplace participation in Loads and Vehicle Financing, improve freight discovery, deepen marketplace liquidity (more shippers and trucks), pursue AI-led faster and smarter freight matching, scale managed fulfilment, and strengthen lender partnerships while maintaining an asset-light approach. Build for Emerging Needs: data-driven product development and expansion into adjacent value-chain services. Power Decisions Through Technology: investment in advanced infrastructure, data science capabilities and analytical tools. On the physical side, the Telematics business is supported by nationwide installation and service infrastructure, and the only capital-expenditure-like disclosure in this bundle is a 'Capital commitments (including purchase of telematic devices)' line - supplied without a printed unit or an attributable period, so its quantum is unusable. Corporate expansion during the year also included the RBI Prepaid Payment Instruments licence to subsidiary TZF (July 03, 2025), the IRDAI Corporate Agent (Composite) registration to BlackBuck Limited (July 31, 2025), and a change of registered office to Koramangala, Bengaluru with effect from May 19, 2026. IPO proceeds remain earmarked against stated objects including sales and marketing, product development, and investment in NBFC subsidiary BlackBuck Finserve to augment its capital base.

verifiable toll, fuel and vehicle tracking data - allows platforms to underwrite commercial vehicle loans for underserved segments.|Structural migration of freight from fragmented broker networks toward trusted technology platforms, improving load discovery, reducing empty runs and increasing realisations for truck owners.|Policy tailwinds: National Logistics Policy, GST-led supply chain formalisation, e-way bill mandates, National Infrastructure Pipeline and PM GatiShakti, plus the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways' aim to bring National Highway logistics efficiency to global standards under the Viksit Bharat vision.

risks.note: Exposure to macroeconomic cycles impacting freight demand, transaction volumes and customer spending; the BRSR adds that a slowdown in economic activity or reduced vehicle movement can affect gross transaction value (GTV), commissions and overall business performance. Management also flags that the ongoing conflict in West Asia may affect freight movement in the near term, which could moderate growth, while expecting the long-term growth trajectory to remain unchanged. Mitigation is revenue diversification beyond core offerings, cross-selling so a downturn in one category is offset by activity in others, and prudent liquidity and cost control.

risks.risk: Business execution risk on the growth businesses
risks.note: The growth strategy depends on successful execution of new initiatives, scaling operations and effective market adoption - the whole Loads and Vehicle Financing thesis sits here. Delays or under-performance in new initiatives could affect projected revenue growth and returns on investments. Mitigated by calibrated investment and phased scale-up, leveraging the existing platform and distribution network, and tracking operating metrics and customer adoption.

Increasing competition from technology platforms, financial service providers and logistics solution providers may impact customer acquisition, retention and pricing; heightened competition could pressure pricing, customer acquisition and retention. Defence rests on differentiation, multi-category cross-selling, an omnichannel service model and continuous competitive analysis.

The business relies on the availability, scalability and reliability of its technology platform to support a growing user base and transaction volumes; platform downtime or scalability constraints could disrupt services, hit transaction volumes and raise remediation costs. Mitigation includes continued investment in scalable architecture to reduce dependency on external technology providers, redundancy in critical IT systems (backup servers, cloud storage, failover), 24/7 monitoring, a dedicated incident response team and a diversified technology vendor base to reduce single-point-of-failure risks.

Increased digitisation exposes the platform to potential data breaches and cyber threats; a breach could result in financial loss, regulatory penalties, litigation and erosion of customer trust - acute for a business holding payment, vehicle-location and credit data. Managed through a cybersecurity framework, periodic internal security audits, access controls and user authentication, a data breach response and recovery plan, and monitoring of data protection regulations.

risks.risk: Financial and regulatory risk, including RBI compliance and partner concentration
risks.note: The Company must implement effective risk management policies, including adherence to RBI regulations applicable to its financial services business, management of partner concentration and maintenance of adequate capital; failure can hamper long-term growth and expansion. Mitigation includes strict RBI compliance reviews, onboarding multiple strategic partners to reduce dependency on key partners, stronger internal financial controls, scenario planning for regulatory change, adequate capital reserves with alternate funding sources, and due diligence on financial partners.

Sustained growth depends on continued customer engagement, service adoption and long-term relationships in a competitive market; loss of customers or lower renewal rates would directly hit recurring subscription and transaction revenues. Addressed through product innovation on affordability and value, bundled offerings across payments, telematics, loads and vehicle financing to drive stickiness, and monitoring of adoption and renewal trends.

The ability to attract and retain skilled talent across technology, product and field operations remains critical for growth; attrition of key talent could increase hiring and training costs and slow execution. The Company notes it ensured continuity in its leadership through managed senior-management transitions during the year, and mitigates through capability and leadership development programmes, career progression pathways, market-competitive compensation, and documented processes with knowledge transfer mechanisms.

one-line thesis: Core businesses (tolling, telematics) delivered 31.5% YoY revenue growth with 94% contribution margin, enabling 51% EBITDA growth despite aggressive superloads expansion into 9 cities; the platform's deep user engagement (45 min/day) and low-cost distribution are creating scalable profitability that funds high-growth verticals with clear path to EBITDA positivity.

segment / subsidiary detail: Core: Tolling revenue grew 24% YoY (GTV +24%, market share compounding); Telematics: highest-ever quarterly sales volume; Growth: Superloads grew 271% YoY (9 cities live), Vehicle Finance grew 35% QoQ (disbursals); Superloads contribution margin high, cohorts break even in 3-4 months, 6-9mo cohorts deliver 30-40% EBITDA

capex / expansion: no formal capex disclosed; heavy investment in superloads via manpower (250+ hires), city ops, tech, and agent networks; no physical asset capex

risks & watch-items: Superloads scaling slower than expected; regulatory changes (wage code impact); competition from unlisted players; platform adoption plateau in mature cities; macro slowdown in CV industry
management quality / tone: Confident, aggressive, and execution-focused; management views superloads as a long-term playbook, not a short-term profit driver; emphasizes platform network effects and operating leverage; no retreat from growth investments post-IPO
non-obvious takeaways: 45 min/day user engagement on app is a defensible moat; 94% contribution margin in core is rare in tech; superloads' 30-40% EBITDA in 6-9mo cohorts suggests path to profitability faster than assumed; off-role manpower model keeps P&L flexible; SME shipper channeling via transporters is a stealth advantage over direct B2B models

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: BlackBuck operates a single mobile application through which Indian truck operators manage the services they use every day - toll and fuel payments, GPS/telematics tracking, freight (loads) discovery and used-commercial-vehicle financing. The Company describes its platform in two parts: Core Businesses (tolling, vehicle tracking, fuel cards and related value-added services, which are high-frequency and recurring) and Growth Businesses (SuperLoads, Vehicle Financing and Loads Classifieds). Customers are truck operators and fleet owners across India's fragmented trucking ecosystem, plus shippers who post freight on the loads platform, served through an asset-light, technology-led and partnership-based model.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Macro backdrop: real GDP estimated to grow 7.7% in FY26 versus 7.1% the previous year, with inflation moderating to 3.4% and the RBI cutting the policy repo rate by 125 basis points; FY27 real GDP growth projected at 6.6% with CPI inflation projected at 5.1%.
- Government capital expenditure as the demand engine: H11.21 lakh crore budgeted towards capital expenditure (3.1% of GDP) with H2.87 lakh crore allocated to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, and the Union Budget 2026-27 raising capital expenditure to H12.2 lakh crore.
- Tolling volume growth directly feeds the Payments business: toll collections increased to H82,342 crore, and FASTag transactions increased to approximately 47,817 lakh during FY26 compared with 41,638 lakh in FY25.
- Structural expansion of the addressable market: India's truck market is projected to increase from USD 25.6 billion in FY 2025 to USD 47.8 billion by FY 2034, a CAGR of 7.16%.
- Fragmentation as the opportunity: road freight accounts for 60-65% of India's freight movement, and the trucking industry remains highly fragmented with a large proportion of operators owning fewer than five vehicles, while rising operating costs, working capital needs and limited access to organised credit accelerate adoption of digital platforms and formal financial services.
- Regulatory mandates pull telematics demand: AIS-140 requires Vehicle Location Tracking devices in public service and commercial vehicles, formalising vehicle tracking as essential infrastructure and expanding the market for telematics and connected-mobility solutions.
- Next leg of tolling digitisation: the transition to barrier-free tolling through ANPR-based systems integrated with FASTag, and the proposed move to Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) and GNSS-based, distance-based toll collection.
- Embedded finance thesis: formalised transport data - verifiable toll, fuel and vehicle tracking data - allows platforms to underwrite commercial vehicle loans for underserved segments.
- Structural migration of freight from fragmented broker networks toward trusted technology platforms, improving load discovery, reducing empty runs and increasing realisations for truck owners.
- Policy tailwinds: National Logistics Policy, GST-led supply chain formalisation, e-way bill mandates, National Infrastructure Pipeline and PM GatiShakti, plus the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways' aim to bring National Highway logistics efficiency to global standards under the Viksit Bharat vision.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Scale leadership: described as India's largest digital platform for truck operators, engaging ~1.1 million truck operators, of whom 818,259 were average monthly transacting truck operators
- Network effects and multi-service stickiness: monthly transacting users using two or more services rose from 259,011 (FY24) to 339,701 (FY25) to 411,765 (FY26)
- High engagement / switching cost: average daily time spent on the app by transacting customers of 43.76 minutes, with the app embedded in daily trucking workflows
- Omnichannel distribution moat: a physical network of over 10,000+ touchpoints with presence across 80%+ districts, complementing digital channels, field sales, telesales and channel partners
- Leadership in commercial vehicle tolling payments - described as the largest tolling platform in India
- Proprietary data advantage across payments, vehicle locations, freight and credit, feeding product development and credit underwriting
- Repeatable playbook for launching new offerings (Payments 2019, Telematics 2021, Loads 2023, Vehicle Financing 2023), lowering incremental customer acquisition cost
- Scalable, asset-light model with in-house microservices technology, recurring revenue and high contribution margins giving operating leverage
- Promoter-led management team and experienced board

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Superloads scaling slower than expected; regulatory changes (wage code impact); competition from unlisted players; platform adoption plateau in mature cities; macro slowdown in CV industry

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: 45 min/day user engagement on app is a defensible moat; 94% contribution margin in core is rare in tech; superloads' 30-40% EBITDA in 6-9mo cohorts suggests path to profitability faster than assumed; off-role manpower model keeps P&L flexible; SME shipper channeling via transporters is a stealth advantage over direct B2B models

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen the core businesses of Payments and Telematics while accelerating investment in the growth businesses of Loads and Vehicle Financing, so that each additional service makes the platform more valuable as operators adopt more offerings.
- Build the digital infrastructure that lets truck operators manage their business and grow their earnings - an ambition explicitly framed as going beyond running successful individual businesses.
- Operating model held constant since inception: identify real customer problems, solve them through a deeply engaged technology platform, and scale them through …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Name change] The covering letter identifies the issuer as BlackBuck Limited, "(Formerly known as Zinka Logistics Solutions Limited)", NSE symbol BLACKBUCK / BSE scrip 544288, ISIN INE0UIZ01018.
- [Unit economics] Contribution margin - defined by the deck as revenue from operations excluding superloads less direct costs of delivering service activities - ran at 93% of net revenues in Q1'FY27, the same as Q1'FY26, versus 94% in Q4'FY26.
- [ESOP] Projected ESOP charge in the P&L tapers from Rs 4.37 Cr in Q2'FY27 to Rs 2.45 Cr in Q4'FY27 and Rs 1.03 Cr by Q1'FY29, projected assuming no further grants and an attrition estimate based on historical and other factors.
- [Headwinds] The deck repeatedly refers to core businesses growing "while navigating industry headwinds" and "despite macro headwinds" without naming or quantifying them.
- [Non-standard measures] The deck reports three overlapping profit measures - EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA (which adds back employee share-based payment expenses) and PAT - each with its own footnoted definition; labels should not be interchanged.
